title: What Is a Programming Paradigm?
learningObjectives: Define the programming approach covered in this lesson.
Identify its main characteristics in an example.
Compare it with another approach where relevant.
Recognize a benefit and a trade-off.
Apply the approach to a small design task.

understand.concept: A programming paradigm is a broad style or approach to organizing and expressing computation. Paradigms influence how programmers model problems, structure code, and reason about behavior. A language may support multiple paradigms, and real programs often combine approaches rather than fitting into one exclusive category.
understand.whyItMatters: Knowing paradigms helps learners recognize alternative designs and choose a style that suits a problem. It also prevents assuming that one language or coding style is the only way to program.
understand.analogy: Different cooking methods are ways to achieve a meal; each method has a different process and focus. Software paradigms are more formal and can overlap within one program.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies the programming model; real code may combine paradigms and language features.

explain.narrative: Read the example and identify how it expresses the task: explicit steps, a desired transformation, named procedures, or objects that combine data and behavior. Paradigms are approaches rather than rigid labels; evaluate the design by clarity and suitability.

commonMistakes: Treating paradigms as mutually exclusive in every program.
Confusing a syntax feature with an entire paradigm.
Choosing a style solely because it is fashionable.

guidedTask.title: Guided practice: What Is a Programming Paradigm?
guidedTask.instructions: Study a small example and identify the design style, its strengths, and its limitations.
steps: Describe the problem the code solves.
Identify the style or paradigm features present.
Trace how data or control moves.
Rewrite or sketch an alternative approach if useful.
Compare clarity and trade-offs of the approaches.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Write a small example illustrating this programming approach.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: paradigm comparison
independentTask.instructions: Create a small solution using the lesson's approach and compare it with a different organization style.
requirements: State the problem and intended result.
Explain which paradigm features you used.
Compare at least one alternative approach.

hints: Paradigms describe organization, not just syntax.
Use the simplest approach that fits the task.
Look for explicit steps versus intent.
Explain trade-offs rather than claiming one style is always best.
